   149	\begin{remark}[Obligations of the linearity-theorem import]
   150		\label{rem:linearity-import}
   151		Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is stated in the form proved in
   152		\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}. Three features are load-bearing for the
   153		proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}: the error is preserved without
   154		polynomial loss ($\delta$ in the hypothesis becomes $\delta$ in the
   155		conclusion); the linearity of the $\{\mathcal{L}^u\}$ is exact and
   156		holds for all pairs $(u,u')$, not merely on average; and the
   157		hypothesis carries no upper bound on $\delta$, so the theorem may be
   158		applied separately for each pair $(x,z)$ with hypothesis error the
   159		conditional linearity defect given $(x,z)$, a quantity for which no a
   160		priori bound is available. The closeness of $\mathcal{L}^u$ to
   161		$\mathcal{O}^u$ is guaranteed on average over a uniformly random $u$
   162		only; this averaged form suffices because the $\mathcal{L}^u$ enter
   163		the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} only through averages over $u$.
   164		The quotation of the theorem in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} differs from the
   165		cited statement in three respects: it inserts the restriction
   166		$0 \le \delta \le 1$, which would block the fiberwise application
   167		just described; it places the closeness conclusion, together with the
   168		exact linearity, under the quantifier ``for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$'',
   169		a strengthening of the theorem proved in
   170		\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; and it appends the identity
   171		$\mathcal{L}^u = \Id$ for $u = 0$. None of the three is reproduced
   172		here: the restriction is dropped, the pointwise closeness is not
   173		used, and the appended identity is instead derived from the
   174		conclusion, since exact linearity at $u = u' = 0$ gives
   175		$(\mathcal{L}^0)^2 = \mathcal{L}^0$, and an idempotent unitary equals
   176		the identity. The import carries two conversion obligations,
   177		discharged in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}: the theorem is
   178		instantiated with $\rho$ the reduced density operator of
   179		$\ket{\hat\psi}$ on the registers carrying the observables, so that
   180		traces against $\rho$ are expectation values in $\ket{\hat\psi}$; and
   181		the correlation hypothesis and the squared-distance conclusion are
   182		converted to and from the relation $\approx_\delta$ of
   183		Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance} by expanding the square, using
   184		unitarity of the observables, and relabelling the averaged index
   185		pair, at the cost of the constant factors absorbed by that
   186		definition. One obligation remains open and is flagged where it
   187		arises: the ancilla register $\hilb'$ and its state
   188		$\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ produced by the theorem, which may depend on the
   189		pair $(x,z)$, must be absorbed --- uniformly in $(x,z)$ --- into
   190		zero-state padding of the strategy state, padding that the source
   191		assumes present without construction.
   192	\end{remark}

   194	\begin{remark}[Normalization of the distance in the linearity conclusion]
   195		\label{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}
   196		The conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} bounds the mean squared
   197		state-dependent operator distance
   198		$\E_u \, d_{\rho'}(\mathcal{L}^u, \mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id_{\hilb'})^2$ by
   199		$\delta$, as quoted in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The calculation behind that
   200		bound in \cite[Section~3.1]{Natarajan2017Linearity} computes the squared

   211		conclusion established by the Fourier argument.
   212	\end{remark}

   385	                        (naimarkAuxProjector α * naimarkAuxProjector α)
   386	                  exact
   387	                    (Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul
   388	                      ρ (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d)
   389	                      (naimarkAuxProjector α) (naimarkAuxProjector α)).symm
   390	        _ = B := by simp [B, haux_idem]
   391	    have hInputProjHerm :
   392	        (oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d))ᴴ =
   393	          oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d) := by
   394	      ext x y
   395	      rcases x with ⟨i, ox⟩
   396	      rcases y with ⟨j, oy⟩
   397	      cases ox <;> cases oy <;>
   398	        simp [oneMeasNaimarkInputProj, oneMeasNaimarkAuxTransition, Matrix.kronecker,
   399	          Matrix.one_apply, eq_comm]
   400	    have hUstar :
   401	        oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d) * Umatᴴ = Vᴴ := by
   402	      have hU' := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose hU
   403	      rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hInputProjHerm] at hU'
   404	      simpa [Umat, V] using hU'
   405	    have hUB : Umat * B = V * B := by
   406	      calc
   407	        Umat * B
   408	            = Umat * (oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d) * B) := by
   409	                rw [hBleft]
   410	        _ = (Umat * oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d)) * B := by
   411	              simp [mul_assoc]
   412	        _ = V * B := by rw [hU]
   413	    have hBUstar : B * Umatᴴ = B * Vᴴ := by
   414	      calc
   415	        B * Umatᴴ
   416	            = (B * oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d)) * Umatᴴ := by
   417	                rw [hBright]
   418	        _ = B * (oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d) * Umatᴴ) := by
   419	              simp [mul_assoc]
   420	        _ = B * Vᴴ := by rw [hUstar]
   421	    have htrace_eq :
   422	        MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (B * Umatᴴ * Q * Umat) =
   423	          MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (B * Vᴴ * Q * V) := by
   424	      calc
   425	        MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (B * Umatᴴ * Q * Umat)
   426	            = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (B * Vᴴ * Q * Umat) := by
   427	                rw [hBUstar]
   428	        _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (Umat * B * Vᴴ * Q) := by
   429	              simpa [mul_assoc] using
   430	                (MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_mul_comm ((B * Vᴴ) * Q) Umat)
   431	        _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (V * B * Vᴴ * Q) := by
   432	              rw [hUB]
   433	        _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (Vᴴ * Q * V * B) := by
   434	              simpa [mul_assoc] using
   435	                (MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_mul_comm (V * B) (Vᴴ * Q))
   436	        _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (B * Vᴴ * Q * V) := by
   437	              simpa [mul_assoc] using
   438	                (MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_mul_comm (Vᴴ * Q * V) B)
   439	    calc
   440	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ρ * M.effect a)
   441	          = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   442	              (oneMeasLiftedDensity α ρ *
   443	                Matrix.kronecker (M.effect a) (naimarkAuxProjector α)) := by
   444	                symm
   445	                exact
   446	                  normalizedTrace_oneMeasLiftedDensity_mul_auxProj (α := α) ρ (M.effect a)
   447	      _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   448	            (oneMeasLiftedDensity α ρ *
   449	              ((oneMeasNaimarkColumn M)ᴴ * Q * oneMeasNaimarkColumn M)) := by
   450	              rw [oneMeasNaimarkCompression (M := M) a]
   451	      _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   452	            ((Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) • (B * (Vᴴ * Q * V))) := by
   453	              simp [oneMeasLiftedDensity, B, V, mul_assoc]
   454	      _ = (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) *
   455	            MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (B * Vᴴ * Q * V) := by
   456	              rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_smul]
   457	              simp [mul_assoc]
   458	      _ = (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) *
   459	            MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (B * Umatᴴ * Q * Umat) := by
   460	              rw [htrace_eq]
   461	      _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   462	            ((Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) • (B * (Umatᴴ * Q * Umat))) := by
   463	              rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_smul]
   464	              simp [mul_assoc]
   465	      _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   466	            (oneMeasLiftedDensity α ρ * (Umatᴴ * Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d)
   467	              (auxProj (some a)) * Umat)) := by
   468	              simp [oneMeasLiftedDensity, B, Q, auxProj, oneMeasNaimarkOutcomeProj,
   469	                oneMeasNaimarkAuxTransition, mul_assoc]
   470	
   471	/-! ### Projective submeasurement on the original outcomes -/
   472	
   473	/-- The completed one-measurement Naimark dilation as a projective
   474	submeasurement on the `Option α` outcome type.
   475	
   476	This is the direct submeasurement interface for the lifted projectors supplied
   477	by `OneMeasNaimarkData`.  The subsequent restriction to the original outcomes
   478	uses `restrictSomeProjSubMeas`. -/
   479	noncomputable def OneMeasNaimarkData.toProjSubMeasOption {α : Type*}
   480	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   481	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   482	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) :
   483	    ProjSubMeas (Option α) (d × Option α) where
   484	  toSubMeas := {
   485	    outcome := data.liftedEffect
   486	    total := ∑ oa, data.liftedEffect oa
   487	    outcome_pos := data.lifted_pos
   488	    sum_eq_total := rfl
   489	    total_le_one := data.lifted_sum_le_one
   490	  }
   491	  proj := fun oa => (data.lifted_isProj oa).isIdempotentElem.eq
   492	
   493	/-- Restrict the completed one-measurement Naimark dilation to the original
   494	outcomes.
   495	
   496	The one-measurement construction gives a complete projective measurement on
   497	`Option α`; the extra outcome `none` carries the residual mass
   498	`1 - ∑ₐ Mₐ`.  Restricting to the `some a` outcomes gives the projective
   499	submeasurement on the original outcome type used by the tensor-product Naimark
   500	statement. -/
   501	noncomputable def OneMeasNaimarkData.toProjSubMeas {α : Type*}
   502	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   503	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   504	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) :
   505	    ProjSubMeas α (d × Option α) :=
   506	  restrictSomeProjSubMeas data.toProjSubMeasOption
   507

     4	/-!
     5	# Naimark rounding of the Fourier-square POVM
     6	
     7	This file carries out the dilation step in the proof of the quantum linearity
     8	theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  The Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2`
     9	of a family of binary observables `O^a`, indexed by the Boolean cube `F_2^t`,
    10	is dilated by the one-measurement Naimark construction of the low individual
    11	degree test to a projective measurement `{C^u}` on the enlarged space
    12	`ι × Option (F_2^t)`, whose compression along the canonical ancillary vector is
    13	again `{B^u}`.  The signed character sums `L^a = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` are then
    14	binary observables satisfying the exact linearity `L^a L^b = L^{a+b}`.
    15	
    16	The one-measurement Naimark construction produces projectors indexed by
    17	`Option (F_2^t)`: one for each Fourier outcome and one for the residual outcome
    18	`none`.  Discarding the residual projector would destroy the resolution of the
    19	identity on the enlarged space, and with it the multiplicativity of the signed
    20	sums.  It is therefore folded into the zero Fourier outcome: the projector
    21	attached to `u = 0` is the complement of the sum of the projectors attached to
    22	the nonzero outcomes.  Since the Fourier-square effects themselves sum to the
    23	identity, the folded projector still compresses to `B^0`.
    24	
    25	## Main definitions and results
    26	
    27	* `naimarkAncilla`, `norm_naimarkAncilla`, `ancProj_naimarkAncilla`: the
    28	  canonical ancillary unit vector and its rank-one density.
    29	* `roundedFourierPVM` with `roundedFourierPVM_isProj`,
    30	  `roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one`, `roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne`, and
    31	  `trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM`: the dilated projective measurement
    32	  and its compression to the Fourier-square POVM.
    33	* `roundedObservable` with `roundedObservable_mul` and
    34	  `roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable`: the exactly linear binary observables.
    35	* `trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedObservable`: the compression of the rounded
    36	  observables, in the form consumed by the averaged distance bound.
    37	
    38	## References
    39	
    40	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, proof of Theorem 10,
    41	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1104`: the Naimark dilation of `{B^u}`
    42	is at lines 1099--1100, the observables `𝒜(a) = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` at lines
    43	1100--1102, and their exact linearity at lines 1103--1104.  The QPBT paper
    44	quotes the theorem at
    45	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`, and
    46	the blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    47	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:98-133`.  The one-measurement
    48	Naimark construction reused here is `oneMeasNaimark` in
    49	`MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/NaimarkOneMeas.lean`, with its data
    50	structure in `MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/Defs.lean`.
    51	-/
    52	
    53	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    54	
    55	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    56	
    57	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    58	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    59	open MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective
    60	
    61	noncomputable section
    62	
    63	/-! ## The canonical ancillary vector -/
    64	
    65	/-- The canonical ancillary vector of the Naimark dilation: the basis vector of
    66	the residual index `none` in `Option (F_2^t)`.  This is the pure state `|anc⟩`
    67	of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`; in the one-measurement
    68	Naimark construction it is the initial state `|⊥⟩` of the auxiliary register. -/
    69	def naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
    70	  EuclideanSpace.single none 1
    71	
    72	/-- The canonical ancillary vector is a unit vector. -/
    73	theorem norm_naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) : ‖naimarkAncilla t‖ = 1 := by
    74	  simp [naimarkAncilla]
    75	
    76	/-- The rank-one density `|anc⟩⟨anc|` of the canonical ancillary vector is the
    77	auxiliary projector `|⊥⟩⟨⊥|` of the one-measurement Naimark construction. -/
    78	theorem ancProj_naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) :
    79	    ancProj (naimarkAncilla t) = naimarkAuxProjector (Fin t → ZMod 2) := by
    80	  ext i j
    81	  cases i <;> cases j <;>
    82	    simp [ancProj, naimarkAncilla, naimarkAuxProjector, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply]
    83	
    84	/-! ## The Naimark dilation of the Fourier-square POVM -/
    85	
    86	/-- The one-measurement Naimark dilation data of the Fourier-square POVM
    87	`{B^u}`, supplied by `oneMeasNaimark`: a family of projectors on
    88	`ι × Option (F_2^t)`, indexed by `Option (F_2^t)`, summing to at most the
    89	identity and reproducing every expectation value of `{B^u}` in the lifted
    90	state.  This is the projective measurement produced by Naimark's theorem at
    91	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`, before the residual outcome is
    92	folded into the zero outcome. -/
    93	def fourierNaimarkData {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    94	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
    95	    OneMeasNaimarkData (Fin t → ZMod 2) ι :=
    96	  Classical.choose (oneMeasNaimark (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement)
    97	
    98	/-- The Naimark dilation data of `fourierNaimarkData` dilates the Fourier-square
    99	POVM. -/
   100	theorem fourierNaimarkData_source {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   101	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   102	    (fourierNaimarkData O hO).source = (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement :=
   103	  Classical.choose_spec (oneMeasNaimark (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement)
   104	
   105	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the rounding below: distinct
   106	projectors of a one-measurement Naimark dilation are orthogonal, since they are
   107	projectors summing to at most the identity. -/
   108	private theorem liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne {α d : Type*}
   109	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   110	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) {a b : Option α} (hab : a ≠ b) :
   111	    data.liftedEffect a * data.liftedEffect b = 0 :=
   112	  data.toProjSubMeasOption.outcome_orthogonal a b hab
   113	
   114	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the compression identities below:
   115	the expectation-preservation identity of a one-measurement Naimark dilation,
   116	written with plain traces.  For every operator `X` on the original space,
   117	`Tr((X ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|) P̂_a) = Tr(X M_a)`. -/
   118	private theorem trace_kronecker_auxProjector_mul_liftedEffect {α d : Type*}
   119	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   120	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) (X : Op d) (a : α) :
   121	    Matrix.trace (Matrix.kronecker X (naimarkAuxProjector α) * data.liftedEffect (some a)) =
   122	      Matrix.trace (X * data.source.effect a) := by
   123	  have h := data.expectation_preservation X a
   124	  simp only [normalizedTrace, oneMeasLiftedDensity, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul,
   125	    smul_eq_mul, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul] at h
   126	  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty d with hd | hd
   127	  · simp [Matrix.trace]
   128	  · have hd0 : (Fintype.card d : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   129	    have hα : (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   130	    rw [mul_comm (Fintype.card d : ℂ), mul_div_mul_left _ _ hα, div_left_inj' hd0] at h
   131	    exact h.symm
   132	
   133	/-! ## Folding the residual outcome into the zero Fourier outcome -/
   134	
   135	/-- The rounded Fourier projective measurement `{C^u}` on `ι × Option (F_2^t)`,
   136	obtained from the Naimark dilation of the Fourier-square POVM by folding the
   137	residual outcome `none` into the zero Fourier outcome.  For `u ≠ 0` the
   138	projector is the dilated projector of the outcome `u`; for `u = 0` it is the
   139	complement of the sum of the dilated projectors of the nonzero outcomes, so
   140	that the family resolves the identity on the enlarged space.  This is the
   141	projective measurement `{C^u}` of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`. -/
   142	def roundedFourierPVM {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   143	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   144	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op (ι × Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
   145	  if u = 0 then
   146	    1 - ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v)
   147	  else (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some u)
   148	
   149	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
   150	dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes absorbs each of them on the
   151	left. -/
   152	private theorem sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   153	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   154	    {v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
   155	    (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) *
   156	        (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) =
   157	      (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) := by
   158	  rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.sum_eq_single v]
   159	  · exact ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some v)).isIdempotentElem.eq
   160	  · intro w _ hwv
   161	    exact liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne _ (fun h => hwv (Option.some_inj.mp h))
   162	  · intro hv'
   163	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hv, Finset.mem_univ v⟩) hv'
   164	
   165	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
   166	dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes is a projector, its summands
   167	being mutually orthogonal projectors. -/
   168	private theorem isProj_sum_erase {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   169	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   170	    IsProj (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) := by
   171	  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
   172	  · unfold IsIdempotentElem
   173	    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   174	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   175	    intro w hw
   176	    exact sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hw)
   177	  · rw [isSelfAdjoint_iff, star_sum]
   178	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   179	    intro w _
   180	    exact ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some w)).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
   181	
   182	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
   183	dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes absorbs each of them on the
   184	right, by taking adjoints in the left absorption. -/
   185	private theorem liftedEffect_mul_sum_erase {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   186	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   187	    {v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
   188	    (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) *
   189	        (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) =
   190	      (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) := by
   191	  have h := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose (sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO hv)
   192	  rwa [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, (isProj_sum_erase O hO).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
   193	    ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some v)).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq] at h
   194	
   195	/-- Every rounded Fourier projector is an orthogonal projection. -/
   196	theorem roundedFourierPVM_isProj {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   197	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   198	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   199	    IsProj (roundedFourierPVM O hO u) := by
   200	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   201	  by_cases hu : u = 0
   202	  · rw [if_pos hu]
   203	    exact (isProj_sum_erase O hO).one_sub
   204	  · rw [if_neg hu]
   205	    exact (fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some u)
   206	
   207	/-- The rounded Fourier projectors resolve the identity on the enlarged space. -/
   208	theorem roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   209	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   210	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, roundedFourierPVM O hO u = 1 := by
   211	  rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ _ (Finset.mem_univ (0 : Fin t → ZMod 2))]
   212	  have hrest : ∑ u ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, roundedFourierPVM O hO u =
   213	      ∑ u ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some u) := by
   214	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   215	    intro u hu
   216	    unfold roundedFourierPVM
   217	    rw [if_neg (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hu)]
   218	  rw [hrest]
   219	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   220	  rw [if_pos rfl, sub_add_cancel]
   221	
   222	/-- Distinct rounded Fourier projectors are orthogonal.  This is the
   223	orthogonality of the projectors `C^u` invoked at
   224	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1103-1104`. -/
   225	theorem roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   226	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   227	    {u v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (huv : u ≠ v) :
   228	    roundedFourierPVM O hO u * roundedFourierPVM O hO v = 0 := by
   229	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   230	  by_cases hu : u = 0 <;> by_cases hv : v = 0
   231	  · exact absurd (hu.trans hv.symm) huv
   232	  · rw [if_pos hu, if_neg hv, Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.one_mul,
   233	      sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO hv, sub_self]
   234	  · rw [if_neg hu, if_pos hv, Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.mul_one,
   235	      liftedEffect_mul_sum_erase O hO hu, sub_self]
   236	  · rw [if_neg hu, if_neg hv]
   237	    exact liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne _ (fun h => huv (Option.some_inj.mp h))
   238	
   239	/-- The compression identity of the rounded Fourier projective measurement: for
   240	every operator `X` on the original space,
   241	`Tr((X ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|) C^u) = Tr(X B^u)`, where `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` is the
   242	Fourier-square effect.  For a nonzero outcome this is the expectation
   243	preservation of the one-measurement Naimark dilation; for the zero outcome it
   244	follows from the resolution of the identity by the `B^u`.  This is the sense in
   245	which `{C^u}` simulates `{B^u}` at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`. -/
   246	theorem trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   247	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   248	    (X : Op ι) (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   249	    Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * roundedFourierPVM O hO u) =
   250	      Matrix.trace (X * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   251	  have hP : ∀ v : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   252	      Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) *
   253	          (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v)) =
   254	        Matrix.trace (X * (operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v)) := by
   255	    intro v
   256	    rw [ancProj_naimarkAncilla]
   257	    unfold heteroKron
   258	    rw [trace_kronecker_auxProjector_mul_liftedEffect, fourierNaimarkData_source]
   259	    rfl
   260	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   261	  by_cases hu : u = 0
   262	  · rw [if_pos hu]
   263	    subst hu
   264	    have hone :
   265	        Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * 1) = Matrix.trace (X * 1) := by
   266	      rw [Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.mul_one, ancProj_naimarkAncilla]
   267	      unfold heteroKron naimarkAuxProjector
   268	      simpa using Matrix.trace_kronecker X
   269	        (Matrix.single (none : Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) none (1 : ℂ))
   270	    have hB : X * (operatorFourier O 0 * operatorFourier O 0) =
   271	        X * 1 - ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, X * (operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v) := by
   272	      rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Matrix.mul_sub]
   273	      congr 1
   274	      rw [eq_sub_iff_add_eq]
   275	      exact (Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ
   276	        (fun v => operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v) (Finset.mem_univ 0)).trans
   277	        (sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one O hO)
   278	    rw [hB, Matrix.mul_sub, Finset.mul_sum, Matrix.trace_sub, Matrix.trace_sub,
   279	      Matrix.trace_sum, Matrix.trace_sum, hone]
   280	    congr 1
   281	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun v _ => hP v)
   282	  · rw [if_neg hu]
   283	    exact hP u

   285	/-! ## The rounded observables -/
   286	
   287	/-- The rounded observables `L^a = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u`, the signed sums of the
   288	rounded Fourier projectors.  These are the observables `𝒜(a)` introduced at
   289	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1100-1102`; the character `(-1)^{u·a}` is
   290	`booleanCharacter u a`. -/
   291	def roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   292	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   293	    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op (ι × Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
   294	  ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • roundedFourierPVM O hO u
   295	
   296	/-- The exact linearity `L^a L^b = L^{a+b}` of the rounded observables, for
   297	every pair of Boolean-group elements.  Expanding the product, the orthogonality
   298	and idempotence of the projectors `C^u` leave only the diagonal terms, and the
   299	characters multiply.  This is the deduction at
   300	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1103-1104`. -/
   301	theorem roundedObservable_mul {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   302	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   303	    (a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   304	    roundedObservable O hO a * roundedObservable O hO b = roundedObservable O hO (a + b) := by
   305	  unfold roundedObservable
   306	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   307	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   308	  intro u _
   309	  rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single u]
   310	  · rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, smul_smul,
   311	      (roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u).isIdempotentElem.eq, ← booleanCharacter_add_right]
   312	  · intro v _ hvu
   313	    rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne O hO hvu.symm,
   314	      smul_zero, smul_zero]
   315	  · intro hu
   316	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ u) hu
   317	
   318	/-- The rounded observable at the zero group element is the identity. -/
   319	theorem roundedObservable_zero {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   320	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   321	    roundedObservable O hO 0 = 1 := by
   322	  simp [roundedObservable, roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one]
   323	
   324	/-- The rounded observables are Hermitian: the characters are real and the
   325	rounded Fourier projectors are self-adjoint. -/
   326	theorem roundedObservable_isHermitian {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   327	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   328	    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   329	    (roundedObservable O hO a).IsHermitian := by
   330	  rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, roundedObservable, Matrix.conjTranspose_sum]
   331	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   332	  intro u _
   333	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_booleanCharacter,
   334	    (roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
   335	
   336	/-- Every rounded observable is a binary observable: it is Hermitian, and its
   337	square is `L^{a+a} = L^0 = 1` by exact linearity. -/
   338	theorem roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   339	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   340	    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   341	    IsBinaryObservable (roundedObservable O hO a) := by
   342	  refine ⟨roundedObservable_isHermitian O hO a, ?_⟩
   343	  have haa : a + a = 0 := by
   344	    ext i
   345	    exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
   346	  rw [roundedObservable_mul, haa, roundedObservable_zero]
   347	
   348	/-- The compression identity of the rounded observables: for every operator `X`
   349	on the original space,
   350	`Tr((X ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|) L^a) = Tr(X ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u)`.  The right-hand side
   351	is the character sum of the Fourier-square POVM whose overlap with `O^a` is
   352	certified by `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`; this is the passage
   353	from `Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` to `Tr_ρ(A(a) ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} (hat A^u)^2)` at
   354	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1105-1110`. -/
   355	theorem trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   356	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   357	    (X : Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   358	    Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * roundedObservable O hO a) =
   359	      Matrix.trace (X * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   360	        (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   361	  simp only [roundedObservable, Finset.mul_sum, Matrix.trace_sum, mul_smul_comm,
   362	    Matrix.trace_smul, trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM]
   363	
   364	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Boolean Fourier analysis for the quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file develops the finite Fourier identities used in the proof of the
     8	quantum linearity theorem.  The Boolean characters are the additive characters
     9	of `𝔽_2^t`; their orthogonality gives Fourier inversion and matrix-valued
    10	Parseval for operator families.  The final section records the normalization
    11	relating the state-dependent operator distance to the distance between the
    12	associated binary projective measurements.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The Fourier and Parseval argument is Theorem 10, equations (7)--(8), and its
    17	proof in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1112`.  The observable-distance
    18	calculation is in the same source at lines 900--912.  The QPBT paper invokes
    19	this theorem in
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-! ## Boolean characters -/
    33	
    34	/-- The character `a |-> (-1)^(a dot u)` on the Boolean cube `𝔽_2^t`.
    35	
    36	This is the scalar character used in the Fourier transform at
    37	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`. -/
    38	noncomputable def booleanCharacter {t : ℕ}
    39	    (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    40	  MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u a
    41	
    42	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    43	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character is
    44	multiplicative in its argument. -/
    45	theorem booleanCharacter_add_right {t : ℕ} (u a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    46	    booleanCharacter u (a + b) = booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b := by
    47	  exact AddChar.map_add_eq_mul
    48	    (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u) a b
    49	
    50	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    51	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: the Boolean pairing defining
    52	the characters is symmetric. -/
    53	theorem booleanCharacter_comm {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    54	    booleanCharacter u a = booleanCharacter a u := by
    55	  simp only [booleanCharacter, MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar_apply]
    56	  have hdot : MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct a u =
    57	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct u a := by
    58	    unfold MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct
    59	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    60	    intro i _
    61	    exact mul_comm _ _
    62	  rw [hdot]
    63	
    64	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    65	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character is
    66	multiplicative in its frequency. -/
    67	theorem booleanCharacter_add_left {t : ℕ} (u v a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    68	    booleanCharacter (u + v) a = booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter v a := by
    69	  rw [booleanCharacter_comm, booleanCharacter_add_right]
    70	  rw [booleanCharacter_comm a u, booleanCharacter_comm a v]
    71	
    72	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    73	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character takes
    74	the value one at the zero argument. -/
    75	@[simp]
    76	theorem booleanCharacter_zero_right {t : ℕ} (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    77	    booleanCharacter u 0 = 1 := by
    78	  change MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u 0 = 1
    79	  exact AddChar.map_zero_eq_one _
    80	
    81	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    82	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character takes
    83	the value one at the zero frequency. -/
    84	@[simp]
    85	theorem booleanCharacter_zero_left {t : ℕ} (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    86	    booleanCharacter 0 a = 1 := by
    87	  rw [booleanCharacter_comm]
    88	  exact booleanCharacter_zero_right a
    89	
    90	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    91	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: every Boolean character
    92	takes values whose square is one. -/
    93	theorem booleanCharacter_mul_self {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    94	    booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u a = 1 := by
    95	  rw [← booleanCharacter_add_right]
    96	  have haa : a + a = 0 := by
    97	    ext i
    98	    exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
    99	  rw [haa, booleanCharacter_zero_right]
   100	
   101	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   102	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: Boolean characters are real,
   103	hence fixed by complex conjugation. -/
   104	theorem star_booleanCharacter {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   105	    star (booleanCharacter u a) = booleanCharacter u a := by
   106	  rcases mul_self_eq_one_iff.mp (booleanCharacter_mul_self u a) with h | h
   107	  · simp [h]
   108	  · simp [h]
   109	
   110	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   111	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: the unnormalized character
   112	sum vanishes away from frequency zero. -/
   113	theorem sum_booleanCharacter {t : ℕ} (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   114	    ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a =
   115	      if u = 0 then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
   116	  rw [show (∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a) =
   117	      (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) *
   118	        𝔼 a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a by
   119	    rw [Fintype.expect_eq_sum_div_card]
   120	    field_simp]
   121	  rw [show (𝔼 a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a) =
   122	      if u = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 by
   123	    simpa [booleanCharacter] using
   124	      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.fourier_fact_vector
   125	        (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u)]
   126	  split_ifs <;> simp
   127	
   128	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   129	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: summing a character over
   130	frequencies gives the delta function at zero. -/
   131	theorem sum_booleanCharacter_swap {t : ℕ} (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   132	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a =
   133	      if a = 0 then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
   134	  simpa only [booleanCharacter_comm] using sum_booleanCharacter a
   135	
   136	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   137	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: orthogonality of two Boolean
   138	characters, in the form used by Fourier inversion and Parseval. -/
   139	theorem sum_booleanCharacter_mul {t : ℕ} (a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   140	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b =
   141	      if a = b then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
   142	  rw [← Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun u _ => booleanCharacter_add_right u a b)]
   143	  rw [sum_booleanCharacter_swap]
   144	  have hab : a + b = 0 ↔ a = b := by
   145	    constructor
   146	    · intro h
   147	      have := congrFun h
   148	      funext i
   149	      have hi := this i
   150	      exact (CharTwo.add_eq_zero.mp hi)
   151	    · intro h
   152	      subst b
   153	      ext i
   154	      exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
   155	  simp only [hab]

   157	/-! ## Operator-valued Fourier analysis -/
   158	
   159	/-- The normalized Fourier coefficient of an operator family on the Boolean
   160	cube.  This is `hat A^u = E_a (-1)^(a dot u) A(a)` from
   161	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`. -/
   162	noncomputable def operatorFourier {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   163	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   164	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op ι :=
   165	  ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   166	    ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • O a
   167	
   168	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   169	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Fourier coefficients of a
   170	Hermitian operator family are Hermitian. -/
   171	theorem operatorFourier_isHermitian {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   172	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   173	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, (O a).IsHermitian)
   174	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   175	    (operatorFourier O u).IsHermitian := by
   176	  rw [Matrix.IsHermitian]
   177	  simp only [operatorFourier, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul,
   178	    Matrix.conjTranspose_sum, star_inv₀, star_natCast]
   179	  congr 1
   180	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   181	  intro a _
   182	  rw [star_booleanCharacter, (hO a).eq]
   183	
   184	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   185	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Fourier inversion for
   186	operator-valued functions on the Boolean cube. -/
   187	theorem operatorFourier_inversion {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   188	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   189	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   190	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier O u = O a := by
   191	  classical
   192	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   193	  have hN : N ≠ 0 := by
   194	    simp [N]
   195	  calc
   196	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier O u =
   197	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   198	          (booleanCharacter u a * N⁻¹ * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
   199	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   200	      intro u _
   201	      simp only [operatorFourier, N, smul_smul, Finset.smul_sum]
   202	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   203	      intro b _
   204	      rw [mul_assoc]
   205	    _ = ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   206	          (booleanCharacter u a * N⁻¹ * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
   207	      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   208	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   209	          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   210	            booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
   211	      rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   212	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   213	      intro b _
   214	      rw [smul_smul, ← Finset.sum_smul, Finset.mul_sum]
   215	      apply congrArg (fun c : ℂ => c • O b)
   216	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   217	      intro u _
   218	      ring
   219	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   220	          (if a = b then N else 0) • O b := by
   221	      congr 1
   222	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   223	      intro b _
   224	      rw [sum_booleanCharacter_mul]
   225	    _ = O a := by
   226	      simp [hN]
   227	
   228	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   229	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: the matrix-valued Parseval
   230	identity for the Boolean Fourier transform.  The order of the two operator
   231	families is preserved. -/
   232	theorem sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   233	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   234	    (A B : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   235	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
   236	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   237	        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   238	  classical
   239	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   240	  calc
   241	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
   242	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ •
   243	          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   244	            (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   245	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   246	      intro u _
   247	      change (N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • A a) *
   248	          operatorFourier B u = _
   249	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul]
   250	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   251	          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   252	      rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   253	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   254	          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   255	      congr 1
   256	      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   257	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   258	          A a * (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   259	            booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier B u) := by
   260	      congr 1
   261	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   262	      intro a _
   263	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   264	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   265	      intro u _
   266	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm]
   267	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   268	      congr 1
   269	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   270	      intro a _
   271	      rw [operatorFourier_inversion]
   272	    _ = ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   273	          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   274	      rfl
   275	
   276	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   277	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Parseval specialized to the
   278	square of a single operator family. -/
   279	theorem sum_operatorFourier_sq {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   280	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   281	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   282	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   283	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   284	        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, O a * O a :=
   285	  sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier O O
   286	
   287	/-- For a family of binary observables, the squares of the Fourier
   288	coefficients sum to the identity.  This is the Parseval step asserting that
   289	`B^u = (hat A^u)^2` is a POVM in
   290	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1100`. -/
   291	theorem sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one {t : ℕ} {ι : Type}
   292	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   293	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
   294	    (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   295	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u = 1 := by
   296	  rw [sum_operatorFourier_sq]
   297	  simp_rw [(hO _).2]
   298	  rw [Finset.sum_const]
   299	  rw [← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℂ]
   300	  rw [smul_smul]
   301	  simp

   303	/-! ## Observable-distance normalization -/
   304	
   305	/-- The affine operator `(1 ± S)/2`, which is the effect of a binary projective
   306	measurement when `S` is a binary observable.
   307	The two effects are `(1 + O) / 2` and `(1 - O) / 2`. -/
   308	noncomputable def binaryObservableEffect {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   309	    [DecidableEq ι] (outcome : Bool) (O : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   310	  if outcome then ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 - O) else ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 + O)
   311	
   312	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance of two operators, summed over the two
   313	effects `(1 ± O)/2`; when both operators are binary observables this is the
   314	squared distance between the associated binary projective measurements.  This is the measurement
   315	distance calculated in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`; its relation
   316	to `stateDepDistSq` is recorded in
   317	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   318	noncomputable def binaryObservableDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   319	    [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
   320	  ∑ outcome : Bool,
   321	    stateDepDistSq (binaryObservableEffect outcome S)
   322	      (binaryObservableEffect outcome T) ρ
   323	
   324	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance is half the squared
   325	state-dependent operator distance.
   326	
   327	**Local fix:** Source equation (3) at
   328	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:903-911` ends by identifying the squared
   329	binary-measurement distance with the squared state-dependent operator distance
   330	of the two observables; the correct relation carries the factor `1 / 2` proved
   331	here.
   332	Documented in
   333	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   334	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two
   335	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) :
   336	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ = stateDepDistSq S T ρ / 2 := by
   337	  simp only [binaryObservableDistSq, Fintype.univ_bool, stateDepDistSq,
   338	    binaryObservableEffect, smul_add, Matrix.conjTranspose_sub,
   339	    Finset.mem_singleton, Bool.true_eq_false, not_false_eq_true,
   340	    Finset.sum_insert, reduceIte, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_inv₀,
   341	    star_ofNat, Matrix.conjTranspose_one, Finset.sum_singleton,
   342	    Bool.false_eq_true, Matrix.conjTranspose_add, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]
   343	  have hminusStar :
   344	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Sᴴ) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Tᴴ) =
   345	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ)) := by
   346	    module
   347	  have hminus :
   348	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - S) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - T) =
   349	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T)) := by
   350	    module
   351	  have hplusStar :
   352	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Sᴴ - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Tᴴ =
   353	        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ) := by
   354	    module
   355	  have hplus :
   356	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • S - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • T =
   357	        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T) := by
   358	    module
   359	  rw [hminusStar, hminus, hplusStar, hplus]
   360	  simp only [neg_mul, mul_neg, neg_neg, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul]
   361	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   362	  ring
   363	
   364	/-- The state-dependent squared distance between binary observables in terms
   365	of their correlation. -/
   366	theorem stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation
   367	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   368	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   369	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   370	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   371	    stateDepDistSq S T ρ =
   372	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   373	  have hstar :
   374	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   375	    calc
   376	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace ((S * T * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   377	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   378	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * T * S) := by
   379	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq, hρ.isHermitian.eq,
   380	          Matrix.mul_assoc]
   381	      _ = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   382	        exact (Matrix.trace_mul_cycle T S ρ).symm
   383	  have hcross :
   384	      (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re = (Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ)).re := by
   385	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   386	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   387	  have hdiff :
   388	      (S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) =
   389	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   390	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq]
   391	    calc
   392	      (S - T) * (S - T) = S * S - S * T - T * S + T * T := by
   393	        noncomm_ring
   394	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   395	        rw [hS.2, hT.2]
   396	        module
   397	  unfold stateDepDistSq
   398	  rw [hdiff]
   399	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   400	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   401	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   402	  rw [hcross]
   403	  ring
   404	
   405	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance is one minus the real
   406	state-dependent correlation. -/
   407	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_one_sub_correlation
   408	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   409	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   410	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   411	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   412	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ =
   413	      1 - (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   414	  rw [binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two,
   415	    stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation S T ρ hS hT hρ htrace]
   416	  ring
   417

     4	/-!
     5	# The operator-valued BLR bound
     6	
     7	This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
     8	linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
     9	indexed by the Boolean cube `𝔽_2^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
    10	operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
    11	family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
    12	sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
    13	overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` used in the
    14	Naimark-dilation argument.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
    15	assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.
    16	
    17	## Main results
    18	
    19	* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
    20	  from `O^{u+v}`.
    21	* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
    22	  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
    23	  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
    24	  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
    25	* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
    26	  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
    27	* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
    28	  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.
    29	
    30	## References
    31	
    32	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
    33	its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
    34	distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
    35	the theorem at
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
    37	invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    38	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81-147`.  The normalization of
    39	the error constant is analyzed in
    40	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
    41	bound is `2 * δ` for the squared state-dependent operator distance
    42	`stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for the squared binary-observable distance.
    43	-/
    44	
    45	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    46	
    47	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    48	
    49	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    50	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    53	
    54	/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
    55	
    56	/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
    57	uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `𝔽_2^t`, of the real part of
    58	`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
    59	Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
    60	quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
    61	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
    62	the one used there. -/
    63	def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    64	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    65	  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    66	    (fun pair =>
    67	      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
    68	
    69	/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
    70	namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
    71	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
    72	`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
    73	quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,
    74	measured with the squared state-dependent operator distance
    75	`stateDepDistSq`. -/
    76	def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    77	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
    78	  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ
    79	
    80	/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
    81	defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
    82	expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
    83	triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
    84	adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
    85	equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
    86	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
    87	family. -/
    88	theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
    89	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    90	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
    91	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    92	    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    93	    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
    94	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
    95	  have hu := hO u
    96	  have hv := hO v
    97	  have huv := hO (u + v)
    98	  have hdiff :
    99	      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   100	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   101	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
   102	      huv.1.eq]
   103	    calc
   104	      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   105	          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   106	            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
   107	        noncomm_ring
   108	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   109	            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   110	        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
   111	        module
   112	  have hstar :
   113	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   114	        Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   115	    calc
   116	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   117	          Matrix.trace ((O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   118	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   119	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * (O v * O u * O (u + v))) := by
   120	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
   121	          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   122	      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   123	        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
   124	  have hcross :
   125	      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
   126	        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by
   127	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   128	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   129	  unfold multiplicativeDefect stateDepDistSq
   130	  rw [hdiff]
   131	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   132	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   133	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   134	  rw [hcross, add_comm v u]
   135	  ring
   136	
   137	/-- The average multiplicative defect over a uniformly random pair equals
   138	`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The pointwise identity
   139	`multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` produces the correlation
   140	summand with the two variables in reversed order; since the pair is uniform,
   141	exchanging the two coordinates leaves the average unchanged.  This is the
   142	relation between the approximate-linearity hypothesis of the QPBT quotation
   143	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`) and
   144	display (7) of Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`),
   145	in the operator-distance normalization of
   146	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   147	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
   148	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   149	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   150	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1) :
   151	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   152	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   153	      2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   154	  have hswap :
   155	      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   156	        (fun pair =>
   157	          (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) =
   158	        blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   159	    unfold blrCorrelation
   160	    refine (avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) _).trans ?_
   161	    exact avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair => rfl)
   162	  calc
   163	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   164	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   165	        avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   166	          (fun pair => 2 - 2 *
   167	            (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) :=
   168	      avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair =>
   169	        multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace
   170	          pair.1 pair.2)
   171	    _ = 2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   172	      rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_uniform_const, hswap]
   173	
   174	/-- The operator-valued BLR bound: under the correlation hypothesis of
   175	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the average squared defect of `O^u O^v`
   176	from `O^{u+v}` is at most `2 * δ`.  This is the passage from display (7) of
   177	Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`) to the
   178	approximate-linearity relation of the QPBT quotation
   179	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`); the
   180	constant `2` is the operator-distance normalization recorded in
   181	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   182	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error {t : ℕ}
   183	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   184	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   185	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
   186	    (δ : ℝ) (hcorrelation : 1 - δ ≤ blrCorrelation O ρ) :
   187	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   188	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) ≤ 2 * δ := by
   189	  rw [avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace]
   190	  linarith
   191	
   192	/-! ## The cubic Fourier identity -/
   193	
   194	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier computations in the
   195	proof of Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick
   196	(`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1112`): a twisted form of the
   197	matrix-valued Parseval identity in which only the first factor is expanded
   198	through its Fourier coefficients.  Taking `a = 0` recovers Parseval. -/
   199	private theorem sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul {t : ℕ}
   200	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   201	    (A X : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   202	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   203	        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =
   204	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   205	        ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   206	          A b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u (a + b) • X u := by
   207	  classical
   208	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   209	  calc
   210	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   211	        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =
   212	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   213	          booleanCharacter u (a + b) • (A b * X u) := by
   214	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   215	      intro u _
   216	      simp only [operatorFourier, N, smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul,
   217	        Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul, booleanCharacter_add_right]
   218	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   219	      intro b _
   220	      congr 1
   221	      ring
   222	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   223	          booleanCharacter u (a + b) • (A b * X u) := by
   224	      rw [← Finset.smul_sum]
   225	      congr 1
   226	      exact Finset.sum_comm
   227	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   228	          A b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u (a + b) • X u := by
   229	      congr 1
   230	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   231	      intro b _
   232	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   233	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   234	      intro u _
   235	      rw [mul_smul_comm]
   236	
   237	/-- The sum of the cubes of the Fourier coefficients of an operator family is
   238	the average of `O^a O^b O^{a+b}` over a uniformly random pair `(a, b)`.  This
   239	is the operator form of the identity
   240	`∑_u (hat A^u)^3 = E_{a,b} A(a) A(b) A(a+b)` invoked at
   241	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1111-1112`; the order of the three factors
   242	is preserved throughout. -/
   243	theorem sum_operatorFourier_cube {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   244	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   245	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   246	        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   247	      ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   248	        ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
   249	          O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
   250	  classical
   251	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   252	  have hinner : ∀ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   253	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   254	          booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
   255	        N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c) := by
   256	    intro b
   257	    rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]
   258	    congr 1
   259	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   260	    intro c _
   261	    rw [operatorFourier_inversion]
   262	  calc
   263	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   264	        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   265	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u 0 •
   266	          (operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   267	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   268	      intro u _
   269	      rw [booleanCharacter_zero_right, one_smul, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   270	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   271	          booleanCharacter u (0 + b) •
   272	            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) := by
   273	      rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]
   274	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   275	          O b * (N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c)) := by
   276	      simp only [zero_add, hinner]
   277	    _ = (N⁻¹ * N⁻¹) • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   278	          O b * O c * O (b + c) := by
   279	      simp only [mul_smul_comm, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul,
   280	        Matrix.mul_assoc]
   281	    _ = ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   282	          ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
   283	            O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
   284	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul, mul_inv]
   285	
   286	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the averages in this file: a uniform
   287	average over a nonempty finite type is the sum divided by the cardinality. -/
   288	private theorem avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum {α : Type*}
   289	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (f : α → ℝ) :
   290	    avgOver (uniformDistribution α) f = (Fintype.card α : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ a, f a := by
   291	  simp [avgOver, uniformDistribution, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight,
   292	    Finset.mul_sum]
   293	
   294	/-- The sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients evaluated in `ρ` equals the
   295	two-query correlation:
   296	`∑_u Re Tr((hat O^u)^3 ρ) = E_{a,b} Re Tr(O^a O^b O^{a+b} ρ)`.  This is the
   297	identity stated at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1111-1112`, with the
   298	complex traces compared through their real parts. -/
   299	theorem operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation {t : ℕ}
   300	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   301	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) :
   302	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   303	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   304	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re =
   305	      blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   306	  rw [← Complex.re_sum, ← Matrix.trace_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul,
   307	    sum_operatorFourier_cube, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul, Finset.sum_mul,
   308	    Matrix.trace_sum]
   309	  unfold blrCorrelation
   310	  rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, smul_eq_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_natCast,
   311	    ← Complex.ofReal_inv, Complex.re_ofReal_mul, Complex.re_sum]
   312	
   313	/-! ## The Fourier-square POVM and its overlap certificate -/
   314	
   315	/-- Each Fourier square `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` of a Hermitian operator family is
   316	positive semidefinite, being the product of a Hermitian matrix with its
   317	adjoint.  This is the positivity half of the assertion that the `B^u` form a
   318	POVM at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1098-1099`. -/
   319	theorem operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef {t : ℕ}
   320	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   321	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, (O a).IsHermitian)
   322	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   323	    (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u).PosSemidef := by
   324	  have h := operatorFourier_isHermitian O hO u
   325	  simpa [h.eq] using
   326	    Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self (operatorFourier O u)
   327	
   328	/-- The Fourier-square POVM `{B^u = (hat O^u)^2}` of a family of binary
   329	observables, with outcomes in `𝔽_2^t`.  Positivity is
   330	`operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef` and completeness is the Parseval
   331	identity `sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one`.  This is the POVM to which Naimark's
   332	theorem is applied at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1097-1100`. -/
   333	def fourierSquareMeasurement {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   334	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   335	    Measurement (Fin t → ZMod 2) ι :=
   336	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   337	    (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)
   338	    (fun u => (operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef O (fun a => (hO a).1) u).nonneg)
   339	    (sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one O hO)
   340	
   341	/-- The effects of the Fourier-square POVM are the squares of the Fourier
   342	coefficients. -/
   343	@[simp]
   344	theorem fourierSquareMeasurement_effect {t : ℕ}
   345	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   346	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   347	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   348	    (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).effect u =
   349	      operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u :=
   350	  rfl
   351	
   352	/-- The average state-dependent overlap between `O^a` and the character sum
   353	`∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u` of the Fourier-square operators `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` equals
   354	the sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients evaluated in `ρ`.  The family `O` is
   355	arbitrary here, so the `B^u` need not be positive or sum to the identity; they
   356	are the effects of a POVM only under the binary-observable hypothesis of
   357	`fourierSquareMeasurement`.  This is the computation of
   358	`E_a Re Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1104-1110`,
   359	carried out before the Naimark dilation: the character sum is the compression
   360	of the exactly linear observable `𝒜(a) = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` to the original
   361	space. -/
   362	theorem avg_overlap_fourierSquare_eq_sum_cube {t : ℕ}
   363	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   364	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) :
   365	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   366	        (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
   367	          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   368	            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) =
   369	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   370	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   371	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re := by
   372	  classical
   373	  have hop :
   374	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   375	          operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
   376	        ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   377	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   378	            booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) := by
   379	    have := sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul O
   380	      (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) 0
   381	    simpa only [booleanCharacter_zero_right, one_smul, zero_add] using this
   382	  symm
   383	  calc
   384	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   385	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   386	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re =
   387	        (Matrix.trace ((∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   388	          operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) *
   389	            ρ)).re := by
   390	      rw [Finset.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum, Complex.re_sum]
   391	      simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
   392	    _ = (Matrix.trace ((((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   393	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   394	            booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) *
   395	              ρ)).re := by
   396	      rw [hop]
   397	    _ = (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   398	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, (Matrix.trace (O b *
   399	            (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u b •
   400	              (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re := by
   401	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul, Finset.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum,
   402	        smul_eq_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_natCast, ← Complex.ofReal_inv,
   403	        Complex.re_ofReal_mul, Complex.re_sum]
   404	    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   405	          (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
   406	            (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   407	              (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) := by
   408	      rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum]
   409	
   410	/-- The overlap certificate for the Fourier-square operators `B^u = (hat O^u)^2`:
   411	under the correlation hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the
   412	average state-dependent overlap between `O^a` and the character sum
   413	`∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u` is at least `1 - δ`.  The family `O` is arbitrary here, so
   414	the `B^u` are the effects of a POVM only under the binary-observable hypothesis
   415	of `fourierSquareMeasurement`.  This is the conclusion of the computation at
   416	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1104-1112` in the form used after the
   417	Naimark dilation: the same overlap, evaluated in `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` against the
   418	exactly linear observables, is what bounds the average distance in display (8).
   419	No commutation among the observables is used. -/
   420	theorem one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare {t : ℕ}
   421	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   422	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι)
   423	    (δ : ℝ) (hcorrelation : 1 - δ ≤ blrCorrelation O ρ) :
   424	    1 - δ ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   425	        (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
   426	          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   427	            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) := by
   428	  rw [avg_overlap_fourierSquare_eq_sum_cube,
   429	    operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation]
   430	  exact hcorrelation
   431	
   432	end
   433	
   434	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
